backtest.assumption_note: Each window is evaluated once, 1 minute after it opens, using the real Kalshi Yes/No quotes at that minute and Coinbase 1-minute / 5-minute / 15-minute / 1-hour BTC candles, plus a spot-derived fair probability from realized 1-minute volatility. Trades use a $4–$8 flat stake by signal strength (no 2× press) and the official quadratic taker fee. When a full 15-minute Kalshi bid path is available, early take-profit and cut-loss rules are applied on that path; otherwise the ticket is held to official Yes/No settlement. The live bot can also enter later in a window (on a 5-minute scan) and uses live order-book and taker-flow data as a market reader; those live-only prints are not in this backtest.
backtest.fee_note: Paper PnL includes Kalshi’s taker fee: ceil(0.07 × contracts × price × (1 − price)), rounded up to the next cent.

strategy.plain_english: Buys Yes/No when the 1-minute trend is clean, BTC is at least $40 from the strike, the ask is 35–75¢, and 2–15 minutes remain in the window. Requires the 50-period EMA to agree. Requires the 5-minute trend to agree. Only buys when the spot-derived fair probability is at least the ask (no overpaying vs fair value). No extra chop filter. Sells early at the live Kalshi bid only when BTC breaks back through the strike and the 1m EMA 9/21 plus MACD both flip against the ticket. Otherwise holds to official settlement.

fee_note: Every paper trade uses Kalshi’s taker fee, ceil(0.07 × contracts × price × (1 − price)), rounded up to the next cent. The Head-to-Head $100 Race starts two books at $100 together (Race 2: Version 1.2 Chart-Confirmed Active vs Version 2.2 Strict + Fair-Value Edge; Race 1 is archived). Existing $40 race books are lifted to $100 by adding the cash delta, so prior trades and P&L stay accurate. The completed 1-hour $40 run and the ongoing $100 book stay in the Trades tab. All books use flat $4–$8 sizing by signal strength (no 2× press). Every ticket costs $4–$8 including fees.

rules_summary.buy_yes: 1m EMA 9 > 21, close > EMA 50, MACD hist > 0, RSI 54–72, 5m trend agrees, BTC at least $40 above the strike, Yes ask 35¢–75¢, and 2–15 minutes left.
rules_summary.buy_no: The bearish mirror (EMA 9 < 21, close < EMA 50, MACD hist < 0, RSI 25–48, 5m trend agrees, BTC at least $40 below the strike, No ask 35¢–75¢).
rules_summary.exits: Sells early at the live Kalshi bid only when BTC breaks back through the strike and the 1m EMA 9/21 plus MACD both flip against the ticket. Otherwise holds to official settlement.
rules_summary.sizing: Normal qualifying signal $4, strong $6, top-conviction $8 — flat $4–$8 per trade (no press). Every ticket’s total cost, including the Kalshi taker fee, stays between $4 and $8. If cash is under $4 the book skips the trade. The $100 race books, the archived 1-hour $40 run, and the ongoing $100 book each use the same flat sizing.
rules_summary.learning: Every hour a GitHub Action studies the last 7–14 days of settled 15-minute windows, walk-forward tests new parameter sets on unseen hours, and only promotes a change when unseen validation dollar P&L is strictly higher than the live config by at least $1.50, overall P&L is positive, and drawdown is acceptable — never just because profit factor rose. That run is free — it does not use Grok Bot.
rules_summary.race: A live Head-to-Head $100 Race compares two books that start together at $100 (Race 2 restarted both at $100 / 0–0 on Nov 27; Race 1 is archived on the Trades tab). Version 1.2 (Chart-Confirmed Active) buys the side BTC is on when the 1m/5m chart score, a $30+ strike gap, a 35¢–65¢ ask, a 15-minute trend that is not against it, and spot fair value ≥ ask all line up — at most one ticket per window and never the opposite side of a held ticket. Version 2.2 (Strict + Fair-Value Edge) follows the learned strategy config, takes at most one trade per window, only when every trend, strike-gap, price, and fair-value filter passes. Both use flat $4–$8 sizing (no press).
